title: Megatron-LM: Training LLMs with Model Parallelism
hook: Split the big matrices inside attention and MLP layers across GPUs, add a few communication ops, and you can train an 8.3B model on 512 GPUs — no custom compiler needed.
key_points: Introduces intra-layer (tensor) model parallelism: split attention and MLP matrices across GPUs.
Implemented with a few communication operations, no custom compiler required.
Trained models up to 8.3B parameters on 512 GPUs.
Set state-of-the-art on WikiText103, LAMBADA, and RACE at the time.
content_html: Mohammad Shoeybi, Mostofa Patwary, Raul Puri, and colleagues at NVIDIA introduced Megatron-LM to push transformer training past what fits on a single GPU. Their approach is intra-layer, or tensor, model parallelism: the large matrices inside the attention and MLP layers are split across GPUs. With this they trained models up to 8.3B parameters on 512 GPUs and set state-of-the-art results on WikiText103, LAMBADA, and RACE at the time.
extra_html:
How it works

Instead of placing whole layers on different devices, Megatron-LM partitions the weight matrices within each attention and MLP block across GPUs, inserting a few communication operations to stitch the results back together. The design needs no custom compiler — it slots into an existing framework — which made the technique easy to adopt.

Why it matters

Tensor parallelism became a core building block of large-model training. The authors report sustaining 15.1 PetaFLOPs across the application at 76% scaling efficiency on 512 GPUs, showing the splits stay efficient at scale. Combined with data and pipeline parallelism, this style of partitioning is how today's largest models are trained.

related.title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations for Trillion-Parameter Models
related.hook: Data-parallel training wastes memory by copying optimizer states, gradients, and parameters onto every GPU. ZeRO partitions them instead — fitting 100B+ parameter models.

related.title: GPipe: Pipeline Parallelism for Giant Networks
related.hook: Spread a network's layers across accelerators as pipeline stages, then split each batch into micro-batches so no accelerator sits idle — near-linear speedup for giant models.

related.title: GPT-3: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
related.hook: Show the model a few examples right in the prompt and it picks up the task — no fine-tuning, no gradient updates. GPT-3 turned prompting into the new programming.
